Plan authored and reviewed to PASS (0 blocking, 1 minor P6 advisory), 1 round, signed at HEAD 1052bc856f.

All three reported reproductions CONFIRMED verbatim on this tree by running the functions:
models_at_or_above("bedrock:us.amazon.nova-pro-v1:0") -> the three bare Anthropic rungs;
largest_window_tokens(same) -> 1000000; models_at_or_above("anthropic:claude-opus-4-8") ->
["claude-opus-4-8"]. Mechanism confirmed at sizing.py:319-327 (fallthrough at :327) and
sizing.py:137-146 (:146).

Two corrections to the original problem statement, both folded into the plan:
- 7de4 is NOT on origin/main. `_rung_target` and tests/unit/test_model_class_ladder.py are both
  absent at HEAD 1052bc856f (7de4 is committed on the unpushed branch feat/7de4-rung-target).
  The plan is therefore written entirely against main and names no 7de4 symbol; the only overlap
  is 7de4s nova start-rung pinning test, which whichever change lands second must update.
- A SECOND call site has the same defect: prerequisites.py:260-261 takes ladder[0] for an
  unlocated primary, so prerequisite-coverage escalation also downgrades and crosses providers.
  The planned models_at_or_above change fixes it without editing that file (its existing
  except (ValueError, IndexError) at :262 turns the resulting IndexError into the explicit
  input-too-large indeterminate at :263). Pinned by a new test rather than assumed.

Separate defect found, NOT ticketed: MODEL_LADDER (sizing.py:99-103) lists claude-sonnet-4-6 and
claude-opus-4-8 at the SAME 1000000 window, so the sonnet -> opus escalation rung buys no extra
context at all. A context-limit escalation that gains zero window is a guaranteed second failure
plus opus pricing. Worth its own ticket.

comments.author: RebarBotNava
comments.body:
CI CAUGHT A REAL DEFECT THAT EVERY LOCAL RUN MISSED — the test edits were never committed.

Gerrit 1230 took a Verified -1. It was NOT a flake, NOT a CANCELLED run, and NOT a coverage-gap
infra -1: the default suite failed identically on ubuntu-py3.11/3.12/3.13 and macos-py3.13, four
platforms, same step, 3 failed / 8858 passed.

THE TELL was in the failing test NAME:
  FAILED tests/unit/test_model_class_ladder.py::test_start_rung_location_for_a_foreign_family_is_unchanged
That name had been RENAMED to ..._is_explicit. CI was therefore running a version of the file that did
not contain the rename. The three failures were the exact pre-fix expectations:
  assert ['bedrock:us.amazon.nova-pro-v1:0'] == ['claude-haiku-4-5', ...]
  assert ['some-unknown-model']              == ['claude-haiku-4-5', ...]
  assert 200000 == 1000000

ROOT CAUSE, verified not guessed:
  git status            ->  M tests/unit/test_model_class_ladder.py
  git show HEAD:tests/unit/test_model_class_ladder.py | grep -c _is_explicit  ->  0
  grep -c _is_explicit tests/unit/test_model_class_ladder.py                  ->  1
The three assertion fixes were edited into the WORKING TREE after the commit was cherry-picked, and
never folded into it. The later cherry-pick of the 77ed commit did not object because it touches a
different file, so nothing surfaced the dirty tree.

WHY LOCAL GREEN PROVED NOTHING: every local run — the 8908-pass run, the mutation check, and the
8909-pass stacked run — executed the WORKING TREE, which had the edits. The pushed commits did not.
Local and CI were testing different trees. This is precisely the "a green suite on a different tree
says nothing about this one" failure mode, and the guard against it is mechanical, not attentional:
ASSERT `git status --porcelain` IS EMPTY BEFORE RUNNING THE SUITE YOU INTEND TO CITE, and again
before pushing. A suite run against a dirty tree is not evidence about the commit.

FIX APPLIED: stash the edit, reset to the 48b3 commit, restore, `git commit --amend --no-edit` (4
files now, was 3), re-cherry-pick 77ed on top. Both Change-Ids preserved
(48b3 Ied2d4002c8e60c2e3085203fa63664ea97639ea8, 77ed Ia9e31b9eac4894871b64504f23c618a21b339976), so
the re-push updates changes 1229/1230 rather than orphaning them. Working tree verified clean, and the
re-verification run records the tree-dirty line count alongside the gate exit codes so the evidence
cannot be separated from the tree it was measured on.

compiled_state.description:
## Context / Problem

`models_at_or_above` (`src/rebar/llm/plan_review/sizing.py:319-327`) locates the ladder START rung
by substring-matching `MODEL_LADDER`'s Anthropic family names (`sizing.py:99-103`) against the
primary model. A primary from any other family matches nothing, falls through to the
`return list(names)` fallback at `sizing.py:327`, and the caller receives the WHOLE ladder from the
trivial rung. `largest_window_tokens` (`sizing.py:137-146`) has the same shape and returns
`MODEL_LADDER[-1][1]` at `sizing.py:146`.

Reproduced on this tree (HEAD `1052bc856f`, no model override, no class table):

    models_at_or_above('bedrock:us.amazon.nova-pro-v1:0')
      -> ['claude-haiku-4-5', 'claude-sonnet-4-6', 'claude-opus-4-8']
    largest_window_tokens('bedrock:us.amazon.nova-pro-v1:0')
      -> 1000000

Contrast, a correctly located primary on the same tree:

    models_at_or_above('anthropic:claude-opus-4-8')                 -> ['claude-opus-4-8']
    models_at_or_above('bedrock:us.anthropic.claude-opus-4-8-v1:0') -> ['claude-opus-4-8']

Two distinct harms:

1. **Escalation DOWNGRADES and jumps provider family.** The Pass-1 escalation loop at
   `sizing.py:378` assigns each returned name straight onto the run config
   (`replace(cfg, model=model)`, `sizing.py:380-386`), so the first "escalation" for a nova primary
   is `claude-haiku-4-5` — a SMALLER window and a different provider than the operator configured.
   The prerequisite-coverage escalation has the same defect through a different expression: it
   calls `sizing.models_at_or_above(model)` at `src/rebar/llm/plan_review/prerequisites.py:260`
   and then takes `ladder[0]` at `:261`, because an unlocated primary is not present in its own
   returned ladder.
2. **The window is overstated.** `ctx.largest_window_tokens` is set from
   `largest_window_tokens(cfg.model)` at `src/rebar/llm/plan_review/orchestrator.py:242` and feeds
   the P8 size budget at `src/rebar/llm/plan_review/det_floor.py:622` and
   `src/rebar/llm/plan_review/pass1.py:388`. So P8 UNDER-blocks: material that will not fit is
   judged to fit, and the review truncates instead of telling the author to decompose.

Who has this, and why now: any operator running the plan-review gate on a non-Anthropic-family
model. The shipped default is the ladder name `claude-opus-4-8` (`src/rebar/llm/config.py:37` and
`:498`), so the defect is invisible on the default configuration and lands exactly on the
deployments that set `REBAR_LLM_MODEL` to their own provider's model — which is the configuration
epic 061c exists to make correct.

## Approach

Make "the ladder cannot locate this primary" an EXPLICIT outcome at both functions instead of a
silent substitution of the whole ladder / the ladder maximum.

- **`models_at_or_above(model)`** — keep both existing branches byte-for-byte: a falsy `model`
  still returns the whole ladder (`sizing.py:327`), and a located family name still returns
  `names[i:]` (`sizing.py:326`). Change ONLY the truthy-but-unlocated case to return `[model]`.
  Worked example, after the change: `models_at_or_above('bedrock:us.amazon.nova-pro-v1:0')` returns
  `['bedrock:us.amazon.nova-pro-v1:0']`. The one-criterion retry still runs, on the operator's own
  model, and there is no higher rung to climb onto.
- **`largest_window_tokens(model)`** — keep the located branch (`sizing.py:141-145`) and keep
  `None` -> `MODEL_LADDER[-1][1]`: with no configured model the gate runs its own default, which
  IS a ladder model, so the ladder maximum is the right answer there. Change ONLY the
  truthy-but-unlocated case to `min(w for _, w in MODEL_LADDER)`. Worked example, after the change:
  `largest_window_tokens('bedrock:us.amazon.nova-pro-v1:0')` returns `200000`, not `1000000`.

**Why `[model]` and not `[]`.** `pass1_with_ladder` has two independent recovery steps: batch ->
one-criterion-per-call (`sizing.py:371-377`), and only then rung climbing. Returning `[]` would
make the `for model in models_at_or_above(...)` loop body never execute, so `produced` stays
`False` and control jumps straight to the `_too_big` failure finding (`sizing.py:401-421`) —
discarding the single-criterion retry, which is the step that most often succeeds because one
criterion is a far smaller prompt than the batch. `[model]` preserves that retry and stops before
the first cross-family rung, so `_too_big` fires only when the criterion genuinely does not fit.

**Why the ladder MINIMUM for an unlocated window.** The two error directions are not symmetric.
Under-blocking is silent: the review proceeds and truncates. Over-blocking is loud and actionable:
P8 emits "reduce/decompose it" with a `_too_big` finding the author can act on. With no window
entry for the operator's model, the honest default is the conservative one. It is also safe for
the other three window consumers — `verify_request_chunks` (`sizing.py:189`),
`pack_prerequisite_bins` (`sizing.py:206`) and `pack_prerequisite_verifier_bins` (`sizing.py:241`)
all divide by this number, so a smaller value yields MORE, SMALLER chunks, never an overflow.

**Why not read the real window from the model profile.** `ModelCapabilities`
(`src/rebar/llm/capabilities.py:30-42`) exposes `native_structured_output`, `prompt_cache_style`,
`supports_thinking` and `supports_temperature` — there is no context-window field. The same
absence is already recorded in-tree at `src/rebar/llm/review_kernel/verify.py:278-281` ("The
ModelProfile capabilities seam ... does not expose max output tokens, so this table is the single
source"). Adding a window to that seam is a larger change across every consumer of
`capabilities_for` (`capabilities.py:221`); this ticket removes the silent WRONG answer using the
machinery that exists, and a profile-sourced window remains available as a later enhancement on
top of an honest fallback.

**Riskiest assumption, tested first.** The assumption most likely to sink this plan is that no
in-tree caller depends on the ladder maximum / full ladder for a truthy unlocated model. Step 1,
before either function is edited, is the cheapest falsifier: run
`grep -rn "largest_window_tokens\|models_at_or_above" src tests` and read every hit. The one known
hit that asserts the behaviour being removed is `tests/unit/test_plan_review.py:1168`; it is
updated in this change (see Scope and Testing). If that grep turns up a production caller that
needs the optimistic value, the fallback is to keep `largest_window_tokens` optimistic and ship
only the `models_at_or_above` half — but the search has already been run once for this plan and
found only the one test assertion.

## Scope

- `src/rebar/llm/plan_review/sizing.py` — `models_at_or_above` (lines 319-327) and
  `largest_window_tokens` (lines 137-146), plus both docstrings, which today say "Unknown/absent
  model -> the whole ladder" (line 321) and "Unknown/absent -> the ladder maximum" (line 140) and
  must state the new unlocated rule. No other function in this file changes, and `MODEL_LADDER`
  (lines 99-103) is not edited.
- `tests/unit/test_plan_review.py` — `test_largest_window_uses_configured_model_window`
  (line 1163): the assertion at line 1168, `largest_window_tokens("some-unknown-model") ==
  sizing.MODEL_LADDER[-1][1]`, pins the exact behaviour being removed and is rewritten to the
  ladder minimum. New regression cases are added beside it and beside
  `test_is_context_limit_error_and_ladder` (line 1123), reusing the module's `_SeqRunner` stub
  (line 1102) and the `orchestrator._models_at_or_above` / `orchestrator.largest_window_tokens`
  re-exports (`orchestrator.py:79` and `:74`).
- `tests/unit/test_plan_review_prerequisites.py` — one new case pinning that the prerequisite
  escalation path stays on the operator's model (see Testing).

**Not edited: `src/rebar/llm/plan_review/prerequisites.py`.** Its escalation at line 260 consumes
`models_at_or_above`, so this change fixes it without touching it: with a returned ladder of
`[model]`, `model in ladder` is true, `ladder.index(model) + 1` is out of range, and the existing
`except (ValueError, IndexError)` at line 262 already converts that into the explicit
`input-too-large` indeterminate record at line 263. That is asserted by a test, not assumed.

**Not in scope: rung TARGET resolution.** Ticket 7de4 changes how a LOCATED rung is NAMED; this
ticket changes only WHICH rung the walk starts from. 7de4 is not on `origin/main` — its symbol is
absent from the tree (`git grep _rung_target origin/main -- src` returns nothing at HEAD
`1052bc856f`) — so this plan is written entirely against main and names no symbol 7de4 introduces.
7de4's plan states it leaves the start-rung behaviour byte-for-byte as it is and adds a pinning
test asserting the nova primary still returns the three bare Anthropic rungs. That pin encodes the
defect this ticket removes, so whichever of the two lands SECOND updates that one assertion to the
new expected value; nothing else in either change overlaps.

## Testing

- **Regression, the exact reported id.** `orchestrator._models_at_or_above(
  "bedrock:us.amazon.nova-pro-v1:0")` equals `["bedrock:us.amazon.nova-pro-v1:0"]`, and no element
  of the returned list contains `"claude-"`. Fails on the current tree, which returns the three
  Anthropic rungs.
- **Regression, the window.** `orchestrator.largest_window_tokens("bedrock:us.amazon.nova-pro-v1:0")`
  equals `200_000` (`min(w for _, w in sizing.MODEL_LADDER)`) and is strictly less than
  `sizing.MODEL_LADDER[-1][1]`. Fails on the current tree, which returns `1_000_000`.
- **Failure path, escalation reports instead of silently crossing families.** Drive
  `orchestrator._pass1_with_ladder` with a `_SeqRunner`-shaped stub (the class at `test_plan_review.py:1102`, extended to record
  `req.config.model`) that raises `Exception("prompt is too long")` at every call (matched by `is_context_limit_error`, `sizing.py:300-316`) and a cfg whose
  model is `bedrock:us.amazon.nova-pro-v1:0`. Assert exactly one finding with `_too_big is True`,
  and assert the models the stub observed are `["bedrock:us.amazon.nova-pro-v1:0",
  "bedrock:us.amazon.nova-pro-v1:0"]` — the batch call plus one single-criterion retry — i.e. the
  run never left the operator's model.
- **Edge, the prerequisite path inherits the fix.** In
  `tests/unit/test_plan_review_prerequisites.py`, following the harness shape already used by
  `tests/unit/test_plan_review_prerequisites_model_log.py:38-77`: monkeypatch
  `sizing.pack_prerequisite_bins` to a single one-block bin, run
  `prerequisites.run_focused_finder` with `cfg.model = "bedrock:us.amazon.nova-pro-v1:0"` and a
  runner that always raises a context-limit error. Assert the runner saw exactly
  `["bedrock:us.amazon.nova-pro-v1:0"]` (no `claude-haiku-4-5` second attempt) and the single
  record is `disposition == "indeterminate"` with the `input-too-large` reason produced at
  `prerequisites.py:263`.
- **Back-compat, located primaries unchanged.** `_models_at_or_above("claude-haiku-4-5")` still
  returns all three rungs in ladder order and `_models_at_or_above("claude-opus-4-8")` still
  returns `["claude-opus-4-8"]` — the assertions already at `test_plan_review.py:1126-1131`, kept
  unmodified. Added beside them: `_models_at_or_above("anthropic:claude-opus-4-8")` and
  `_models_at_or_above("bedrock:us.anthropic.claude-opus-4-8-v1:0")` both equal
  `["claude-opus-4-8"]`, and `largest_window_tokens` is `1_000_000` for `"claude-haiku-4-5"` and
  `"claude-opus-4-8"` (lines 1165-1166, unmodified).
- **Back-compat, no configured model.** `_models_at_or_above(None)` still returns all three rungs
  and `largest_window_tokens(None)` still equals `sizing.MODEL_LADDER[-1][1]` (line 1167,
  unmodified).

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] For a primary the ladder cannot locate, no proposed rung has a smaller window than the
      primary's, because the only proposed rung is the primary itself: verified by a new test
      asserting `orchestrator._models_at_or_above("bedrock:us.amazon.nova-pro-v1:0") ==
      ["bedrock:us.amazon.nova-pro-v1:0"]` and that no returned element contains `"claude-"`,
      which fails against the current tree.
- [ ] `largest_window_tokens` no longer returns the ladder maximum for a model absent from the
      ladder: verified by a new test asserting
      `orchestrator.largest_window_tokens("bedrock:us.amazon.nova-pro-v1:0") == 200_000` and
      `< sizing.MODEL_LADDER[-1][1]`, plus the rewritten assertion at
      `tests/unit/test_plan_review.py:1168` for `"some-unknown-model"`.
- [ ] A non-Anthropic-family primary that context-limits at every attempt still produces the
      existing `_too_big` failure finding rather than an empty result or a raised exception, and
      the escalation never leaves the operator's model: verified by the new `_pass1_with_ladder`
      test asserting `finding["_too_big"] is True` and that the observed model list is exactly
      `["bedrock:us.amazon.nova-pro-v1:0", "bedrock:us.amazon.nova-pro-v1:0"]`.
- [ ] The prerequisite-coverage escalation (`prerequisites.py:260-263`) stops on the operator's
      model instead of jumping to `claude-haiku-4-5`, with `prerequisites.py` itself unedited:
      verified by the new `run_focused_finder` test asserting the runner saw only
      `["bedrock:us.amazon.nova-pro-v1:0"]` and returned an `indeterminate` record, and by
      `git diff --stat` showing no change to `src/rebar/llm/plan_review/prerequisites.py`.
- [ ] Behaviour for an Anthropic-family primary is unchanged, qualified or bare: verified by
      `test_is_context_limit_error_and_ladder` (`test_plan_review.py:1123`) passing unmodified,
      by `largest_window_tokens(None) == sizing.MODEL_LADDER[-1][1]` (line 1167) passing
      unmodified, and by new assertions that `_models_at_or_above("anthropic:claude-opus-4-8")`
      and `_models_at_or_above("bedrock:us.anthropic.claude-opus-4-8-v1:0")` both equal
      `["claude-opus-4-8"]`.
- [ ] `MODEL_LADDER` is not edited: verified by `git diff src/rebar/llm/plan_review/sizing.py`
      showing no change to lines 99-103.
- [ ] `make lint` and `make typecheck` exit 0, and `pytest tests/unit/test_plan_review.py
      tests/unit/test_plan_review_prerequisites.py
      tests/unit/test_plan_review_prerequisites_model_log.py tests/unit/workflow/test_pass1_usage.py
      tests/unit/workflow/test_review_output_budget.py` passes, as does the default test selection.

compiled_state.title: Context-limit escalation mis-locates the START rung for a non-Anthropic-family primary: it downgrades the window and jumps provider family
